hits.name: Argona
hits.text:
i gave Jev + Astra 6 a dead tiktok account and told it "make money or i'll delete you"

11 days later it's booked $4,200 in brand clips

and i still haven't opened the app

this isn't a wrapper. i trained the model in the video myself. 22,045 weights, 6 blocks, it learns which 4 opening frames hold a thumb. jev labels its food, astra 6 wrote its training loop

every 30 minutes it:

→ pulls the 800 to 1,200 clips posted in my niche in the last 6 hours
→ labels every one of them with jev: hook type, pacing, why it held or lost. 1,200 clips costs 8 cents
→ keeps only the ones that beat their own channel's median, so a small account winning counts more than a big one coasting
→ feeds those into my model overnight, 4 frames at a time, loss 1.3534 and falling
→ has astra 6 build the 3 best ideas into finished clips, hook, shot list, cover, captions
→ posts them and pays its own render bill out of what they earn

if a clip is under 41% retention at one hour, the idea is deleted and never proposed again

if the render budget hits $0, it stops posting

so it learned what survives

the numbers nobody puts side by side:

jev never writes a word, it only picks, in 70 to 500 ms. $0.042 per million tokens in, and the answers are free, which is why labelling a whole niche costs less than a coffee

astra 6 holds 1,050,000 tokens and lands 88% of jobs first try, 99.2% inside four

past 272,000 tokens astra's price doubles, so jev keeps its context starved on purpose

tool calls fail 3 to 15% of the time, so exactly one process in the whole thing is allowed to publish. everything else can only propose

it only ever copies structure, never words. the first 1.2 seconds, the cut rhythm, where the face enters. that's the part that transfers between niches

$0 to $4,200 in 11 days, on an account i'd already buried

how much do u think it does in a month?

CLAUDE + OBSIDIAN + KARPATHY'S LLM WIKI = A WIKI THAT MAINTAINS ITSELF

run this once and your research compounds instead of evaporating

sources go in, a wiki comes out, and a loop keeps it honest

• three layers, one owner each
> the schema - CLAUDE.md, you and the agent co-evolve it
> the wiki - markdown the agent owns. it writes, you read
> raw sources - immutable, read only, never edited

• three operations on repeat
> ingest - read the source, write the summary, log one line
> query - answer with citations, file it back as a new page
> lint - contradictions, orphans and dead links caught early

RAG re-derives the same answer from raw chunks on every query. you pay for that thinking again, every time you ask

this wiki gets written once and stays current. 10-15 pages per source, nearly 100 sources on the index alone

month one it saves you an hour a day. month six it knows your field better than the person you're up against for the senior seat

"Obsidian is the IDE, the LLM is the programmer, the wiki is the codebase" - Andrej Karpathy

hits.text:
this JEV + Picsart split is f**king insane for AI workflows

so i rebuilt one campaign around a simple rule: cheap decisions happen before expensive generation.

[here’s what’s actually happening:]

1. JEV sits in front of the stack and decides `allow_subagent`, `ask_human`, `stop_retry` or `reuse_cache` before anything expensive runs.

2. Picsart handles the heavy work across 188 models from 34 providers for image, video, audio and editing.

3. every output gets reviewed before the next expensive step is allowed to run.

4. if one stage fails, JEV keeps 5 finished stages cached and reruns only the broken branch.

5. 11 JEV decisions cost $0.0011 in this setup. the same decision loop through an LLM would be around $0.33.

6. the pipeline becomes: decide → generate → review → reuse → rerun only what failed.

the interesting part is not adding another agent.

it is stopping expensive models from doing work a $0.0001 decision could have prevented.

9 → safeguards are strict: cyber-adjacent tasks get bounced to Opus 4.8 even when it's not security work. doing real security? apply to the Cyber Verification Program

10 → real-world numbers: a 200k-line codebase audit in under 3 hours (Opus 5 took 20+ hours and 2.5x the tokens). HAProxy rewritten from C to Rust in 9.5h vs 12h on Fable 5.1, 51% cheaper

the result: Fable-level intelligence on your subscription at Opus prices, as long as you run High and leave Max alone

Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 are coming in the next few weeks. bookmark this before your first Max run eats your week
